name: sc-loans-vo-1
text: Paying EMIs... for a flat that never came? [short pause] On Thursday, the Supreme Court stepped in. Twice. First, Sonipat. Buyers signed a three-way loan deal: buyer, builder, bank. The project stalled. The builder went into insolvency. And the bank came after the buyers. The court said: no coercive recovery... until a court checks two things. Did the buyers really default? And did the bank pay the builder the way the deal said? Because in a three-way loan, the money is meant to go in stages... as the building rises. Not all at once. Same day, Bengaluru. About four thousand five hundred buyers, who had paid about ninety-five percent of the price. The order: no coercive measures... till they get their flats. But the court also warned: not every failed project belongs in the Supreme Court. Go to the High Court or the tribunal first. So when a project stalls... who should carry the risk? The buyer, or the bank?
